article.title: Замороженные ягоды и норовирус: как общая партия связала вспышки на судах
article.scope: Полный перевод основной статьи на 2 журнальных страницах: все 4 абзаца расследования, благодарности, сведения об авторах и организациях, данные для переписки, заявление о конфликте интересов и сноска. Все 3 библиографические записи сохранены на языке оригинала. В источнике нет отдельной аннотации, рисунков и таблиц. Текст подготовлен по полному XML PMC и сверён с PDF издателя. Подзаголовки добавлены для навигации; редакционные пояснения отделены от перевода.

source.license: Public domain, explicitly stated in article-specific PMC XML license paragraph and MMWR policy. XML also carries a CC BY 3.0 text-mining reference.
source.rights_note: Attribution, free-source link and nonendorsement notice supplied. Publisher PDF bytes preserved. Translation, added navigation subheadings and separate editorial explanations identified; no CDC logo introduced.
source.status_check: Publisher page has no correction notice; Crossref has no update-to relation and XML has no retracted-article relation. Targeted DOI correction search and PubMed did not reveal a correction.

selection.reader: Food safety, HACCP, laboratory, purchasing and supplier-control teams handling frozen fruit and berries.
selection.utility: Shows how repeated outbreaks were connected through ill-passenger questionnaires, lot-number matches, food testing and supply records across an entire fleet.
selection.limits: Historical 2019 outbreaks; source published April 24, 2020. Detailed counts cover three voyages of two ships, not all summer outbreaks on ten ships. Nearly 80% refers to completed questionnaires from ill passengers with no total questionnaire denominator or non-ill comparison. Stool genotype GII.2[P16], food genogroups II versus I, and 97.5% sequence similarity are distinct results. PCR is not a viability test. No further outbreaks reported after removal is observational; no disinfection protocol or current recall inferred.

review.numeric_literals: pass; English thousands separators and Russian grouping spaces normalized separately from decimal commas
review.arithmetic: All six passenger/crew percentages agree with one-decimal rounding. Stool submissions 4+5+2=11, positives 3+4+2=9. No denominator supplied for nearly 80% of food questionnaires; no attack rate inferred from that fraction.
review.spelled_numbers: Four stools with three positives on first A voyage; five with four positives on B; two with two positives on second A voyage. Three voyages on two ships distinguished from summer outbreaks on ten ships. Sixteen food items tested; three positive with genogroups II, I, I. Stool genotype GII.2[P16], 97.5% sequence similarity and nearly 22,000 pounds preserved.
review.pdf_visual_review: All four pages inspected. Source text, author details, references and attribution legible; separate introductory page for editorial notes.

typesafe.mode: Additional review for coverage; full source comparison retained. No efficiency claim.
typesafe.manual_review: All three accepted source/translation pairs and negative control assessed manually: 80% of completed ill-passenger questionnaires, nine of eleven stool positives, distinct food genogroups, 97.5% similarity, historical supplier traceback and absence of further reported outbreaks retained. No automatic acceptance based on model labels.
